exposure: Placenta accreta spectrum (placenta accreta, percreta, partial accreta)
outcome: Neonatal clinical outcome (fetal weight, Apgar score)
cohort: The study included 58 cases of sonographically diagnosed, clinically managed, and pathohistologically confirmed placenta accreta spectrum, compared to a control group of 135 cases with normal placenta.
finding: The primary findings were that previous caesarean section and placenta previa were the main risk factors for placenta accreta, which was associated with a high peripartal hysterectomy rate (91%), significant surgical complications (uterovesical lesions, excessive haemorrhage), increased blood loss, more resuscitation measures, and longer hospital stays, while neonatal outcomes were generally good.
mod_finding: Blood loss was higher in groups with emergency hysterectomy and relaparotomy (3510-6500 ml) compared to planned delivery with caesarean hysterectomy due to placenta accreta (3420 ml).
